children: JM Financial expects strong cargo growth at Adani Ports and JSW Infrastructure, while softer export-import volumes could weigh on Concor and non-aeronautical revenue is likely to support GMR Airports

India’s ports, logistics and airport operators are expected to report a mixed performance in the second quarter of FY27, with healthy cargo demand supporting major port operators even as container volumes remain subdued at Container Corporation of India (Concor) and passenger traffic growth at GMR Airports faces a temporary slowdown.

According to a quarterly preview by domestic brokerage JM Financial, Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) is expected to lead operational growth, supported by strong domestic demand and favourable pricing. JSW Infrastructure is also projected to report higher cargo volumes, while Concor could face pressure on earnings. GMR Airports is expected to rely on its non-aeronautical businesses to support profitability.
The outlook reflects resilience in core operational metrics despite macroeconomic headwinds and geopolitical disruptions, according to the brokerage’s assessment published on October 12.
Adani Ports Set For Strong Quarter
Adani Ports is expected to report cargo volumes of around 142 million metric tonnes (MT), representing a 15.2 per cent year-on-year increase, according to JM Financial.

The brokerage estimates revenue at Rs 11,193.3 crore and adjusted profit after tax (PAT) at Rs 4,032.7 crore. Core earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) are projected at Rs 6,694.4 crore, implying a margin of 59.81 per cent.

Strong domestic operations are expected to support the company’s growth trajectory and could provide scope for it to exceed its annual targets. JM Financial said a potential increase in the company’s Ebitda guidance could also be considered during its upcoming earnings call.
JSW Infrastructure Sees Volume And Revenue Growth
JSW Infrastructure is expected to maintain its growth momentum despite disruptions at Fujairah port linked to the West Asia crisis.
JM Financial forecasts cargo volumes to increase 8.5 per cent year-on-year to 29.5 million MT, supported by a sharp rise in third-party coastal coal cargo.
Revenue is projected to grow 15.5 per cent to Rs 1,461.6 crore, while PAT is estimated at Rs 392 crore. Ebitda is expected to reach Rs 651 crore, translating into a margin of 44.5 per cent.
The brokerage noted that the company's logistics business continues to provide support to its financial performance.
Concor Faces Pressure From Softer Volumes

Concor is expected to report relatively subdued operational performance, with export-import (EXIM) container handling projected to grow 3.1 per cent year-on-year to 1.13 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs).

JM Financial estimates Ebitda to decline 8.8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 518.9 crore, with margins at around 21.3 per cent. Revenue is projected at Rs 2,431.7 crore, while PAT is estimated at Rs 327.7 crore.
Despite the expected earnings pressure, the brokerage sees the company's pricing strategy as a potential advantage in gaining market share from road transportation.
Non-Aeronautical Business To Support GMR Airports
GMR Airports is expected to depend on its non-aeronautical revenue streams to support margins as passenger traffic growth remains muted in the near term.
JM Financial expects a meaningful recovery in passenger traffic growth only in the third quarter of FY27, despite the addition of new airports to the company's portfolio.
For the second quarter, revenue is projected to rise 8.2 per cent year-on-year to Rs 3,972.2 crore. Ebitda is estimated at Rs 1,519.6 crore, with a margin of 38.3 per cent.
The company is also expected to return to profitability, with projected PAT of Rs 143.8 crore against a net loss in the corresponding quarter last year.
Sector Outlook Hinges On Cargo Demand

The Q2FY27 outlook points to divergent earnings trends across India's ports and logistics sector. Strong cargo volumes and domestic demand are expected to benefit major port operators, while subdued container growth could weigh on Concor's earnings.
For airport operators, the ability to grow non-aeronautical revenue is expected to remain important in sustaining financial performance until passenger traffic growth strengthens.
